page.layout: One printed page (book page 92). Running head at top centre-right. One main text column. Two marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines "lectusdicantur" and "naturaliter vivens". Catchword "mente" at bottom right. No text in the right margin apart from show-through from the facing page, which is left out.

main_text.p: concipere licet. Ita solet plerumque argumentari, & fungi tales dantur, qui nec Philosophos nec Theologos genuinos unquam legerunt, quibus interim oracula fundere videtur iste, magnus sc Philosophus. Sed pergat. Nam quandoquidem hic sermo est de cognitione vera, nulla ratione concipere licet; quomodo cognitio alicujus rei vera, possit esse tenebrae: at bone vir quis unquam ullam cognitionem veram, aut absolute, aut in quantum vera est, tenebras dixit? nemo tam bardus est, quanquam tacitè aliis tantam stupiditatem imputare studeas. An nescis distinguere genus à genere, spirituale à naturali, regenitum ab irregenito? an non potest esse, vera rerum naturalium, terrenorum, quaedam cognitio, qua non obstante, respectu spiritualium, spiritualis quo ea concipiuntur modi homo ejusque intel-lectus dicantur tenebrae? & mente excaecati? quasi Eph.v.4.lectusdicantur tenebrae? & mente excaecati? quasi naturaliter vivens, spiritualiter mortuus & à vita Dei alienatus dici, nequeat? quasi quaedam naturalia, terrena dicit Velthuisen, verè per naturam cognoscentes, mentè excaecati dici non possint? Verum falleris vehementer, aut Ephesii omni modo mortui, eorumque Doctissimi omni modo amentes, ex tua sententia fuerunt ante conversionem: erant enim, Apostolo judice, non obstante vita naturali mortui spiritualiter, & non obstante etiam vera quorundam terrenorum cognitione, olim mente excaecati, imo tenebrae. Quorsum igitur haec verba, sc. ut ne alia, praeter τὸ[?], non licet concipere, desit ratio: cum utraque cognitio tam spiritualium quam rerum terrenarum sit à Deo, sit veritas, sit regula ad quam homines rectè vitam suam componunt &c. quid inde? nihil aliud, quam, quod naturaliter verum est illud revera verum esse & merito pro vero haberi. At longe aliud quid hinc extundet Medicus. Propter eadem, inquit, rationes unum tantum luminis genus mente

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Eph.v.4." and "IV.18." (printed "IV.18.") beside lines 16 and 17 of the paragraph; the note "IV.18." is set beside "naturaliter vivens" and is kept in the margin, not in the text. The Greek word after "praeter" is printed as τo with an accent mark; read as τὸ with doubt. The word "bardus" and the "sc" after "magnus" are as printed. The word "genus" at the end of the line "eadem, inquit" is roman and appears to close the line rather than being a catchword. The catchword "mente" is at bottom right. Show-through from the facing page on the right is not transcribed. The note "IV.18." is marked as a margin note; its exact position was not fully clear at this resolution.
